clozapine.t: Concomitant use of clozapine and LOREEV XR may produce marked sedation, excessive salivation, hypotension, ataxia, delirium, and respiratory arrest.
Concomitant use of clozapine and lorazepam may produce marked sedation, excessive salivation, hypotension, ataxia, delirium, and respiratory arrest.

valproate.t: Concurrent administration of lorazepam with valproate results in increased plasma concentrations and reduced clearance of lorazepam.
Lorazepam dosage should be reduced to approximately 50% when coadministered with valproate.

valproic acid.t: Concurrent administration of lorazepam with valproate results in increased plasma concentrations and reduced clearance of lorazepam.
Lorazepam dosage should be reduced to approximately 50% when coadministered with valproate.

theophylline.t: Administration of theophylline or aminophylline may reduce the sedative effects of benzodiazepines, including lorazepam.

opioid.t: Prescribe the lowest effective dosage; avoid or minimize concomitant use of CNS depressants and other substances associated with abuse, misuse, and addiction (e.g., opioid analgesics, stimulants); and advise patients on the proper disposal of unused drug.
ABUSE, MISUSE, AND ADDICTION; and DEPENDENCE AND WITHDRAWAL REACTIONS Concomitant use of benzodiazepines and opioids may result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death.

anticonv.t: The benzodiazepines, including Lorazepam, produce increased CNS-depressant effects when administered with other CNS depressants such as alcohol, barbiturates, antipsychotics, sedative/hypnotics, anxiolytics, antidepressants, narcotic analgesics, sedative antihistamines, anticonvulsants, and anesthetics.
